newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Full EU tax harmonisation undesirable - Monti.
newsitem.headline: Full EU tax harmonisation undesirable - Monti.

text.p: European Union Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti made clear on Saturday he did not want to see a full harmonisation of national tax systems.
Monti, taking part in the informal Industry Council, said noone would be in favour of that.
"It would not only be highly unrealistic but also in my view totally undesirable," Monti told a press conference.
For example, he said personal income taxation was a "typical field for subsidiarity" and that differences between member states did not hurt the single market.
In contrast, systems for Value Added Tax (VAT) could hurt the single market if they were complex and not sufficiently harmonised, he said.
In between those two extremes, Monti said that in his view taxation on capital income required coordination, if not harmonisation.
Taxation measures will be included in the Commission's planned action plan for the completion of the single market, due to be put forward at the EU summit in Amsterdam in June.
